gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-graduate: Dignified and bookish, Graduate gives its serif letters plenty of white between them, with lowercase barely shorter than capitals. Conthrax, geometric and clean, runs the same way, so the two feel like cousins from different eras.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-roboto: Conthrax is wide and geometric, with no swells to slow the eye. Roboto has generous round letters and little gap between capitals and lowercase, so a full page of it moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-conthrax-switzer: Switzer draws wire-like, tubular letters with a tall waist line and c tips that never creep toward touching. Beneath the Conthrax heading, extended reading stays smooth, approachable, and Swiss in feel.
gen-dafont-cookies-fs-karma: Karma reads smoothly, its modulation never snagging the eye. Cookies is best at being sweet and inviting, with a huge lowercase eye, while Karma does its best work staying trustworthy and classic.
gen-dafont-cookies-montserrat: Pinched meets spacious: Cookies cuts its apertures razor-slim, while Montserrat lets every curve open up with oversized counters. That closed-against-open difference is the pair's real draw, sweet above and approachable below.
gen-dafont-cowboys-crimson-pro: Rustic and authoritative, Cowboys spaces its stems far apart and traces each letter in one flat, unmodulated line. But Crimson Pro, a refined serif, does its best work with a gently modulated cadence across tightly packed lines.
gen-dafont-cowboys-fs-alpino: This body text reads cozy and casual, tightly spaced, with ascenders that look short because the letters are so tall. Alpino packs its letters tightly while Cowboys leaves wide gaps, and that tension is the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-cowboys-fs-fira-sans: A constant-width trace, like a laser-etched line, gives Cowboys its rustic, authoritative look. And Fira Sans, a professional sans with a larger-than-usual x-height, feels like firm ground beside those spaced-out stems.
gen-dafont-cowboys-fs-hind: Cowboys traces each letter like a laser-etched line, with big gaps between stems, while Hind keeps its lowercase close to capital height. Cowboys earns its keep when it is big and brief.
gen-dafont-cowboys-fs-karma: Cowboys draws a constant-width line, like laser etching. Karma, a trustworthy serif whose lowercase sits close to the capitals, wants a generous size to let its calm modulation show.
